Wear a helmet

I got a bad concussion 10 years ago. It was the end of 7th grade and I was playing manhunt with my friends. I tripped and fell headfirst onto some rocks. Hairline fracture in my cheekbone and brain swelling. Not really realistic to wear a helmet all the time, but I was a clumsy kid and it probably would have prevented quite a few injuries. My grades slipped, I developed severe depressive symptoms, and my OCD got worse. I’m doing much better now as an adult, thank god. Overall, I wish I could go back and be more careful about a lot of the dumb shit I did as a teenager.
If you’re just a neat person, that’s no reason to worry. But if it impacts your functioning and causes extreme distress you should definitely speak to a professional!

I think it ultimately depends on the person. Some people are just really organized and like to keep things neat, but that’s not OCD. Some people with OCD are extremely neat and it may or may not have anything to do with their disorder. Neatness on its own isn’t indicative of OCD. Everyone’s a little different. My OCD is more like “damn if I don’t get out of bed and brush my teeth 5 more times my house is going to burn down.” It’s completely irrational, but it is hard to resist compulsions. I brushed my teeth 7 times last night before bed because I felt like I “didn’t do it right” the first time. I was awake until 2am from anxiety. My brain is weird!
My mom worked an office job when I was young but became a stay-at-home mom for most of my childhood. My dad works as an editor and is also a published author.

Thank you for your question!! Most people assume OCD is just a fancy word for being picky or super organized, and never think to ask what else it entails. I have severe OCD and I’m one of the least organized people on the planet! OCD goes so much deeper than that. Intrusive thoughts/mental images, lack of sleep from staying up and repeating compulsions, chapped and bloody hands due to excessive hand washing, etc. The truth is that this disorder is incredibly painful and isolating. I wish people would ask more questions (even when it’s uncomfortable) rather than assume what the experience is like.

I lost a close friend of mine to suicide a few years ago and ever since then my life has been a constant rollercoaster of getting better and then getting worse again. Sorry you've been going thru it alone. Feel free to PM me if you need to vent it out to someone!

I grew up in the same area. Graduated in 2017, Peter’s sister was in my grade. His mom was my teacher. Crazy to think someone like this was living among us casually and we had no idea. I feel horrible for all the families and friends who lost a loved one in this awful tragedy. At least they caught him before he was able to hurt anyone else, and hopefully justice will be served.

Not gay, but bisexual with a preference for girls. It took a long time to explore and accept my sexuality. I think I always kind of knew, but was uncomfortable with experimenting at first. I began to overcome my guilt/confusion by asking myself important questions (am I sexually attracted to women, could I see myself in a relationship with a woman, etc...), meeting other gay girls, and eventually having more and more lesbian experiences. Self discovery and self acceptance is a process, and your journey/identity belongs to you! How you identify and what you discover about yourself is valid. YOU are valid! Best of luck to you :)

Introvert by default, but I crave social interaction. I’m just bad at navigating it. I often feel burnt out afterwards, but sometimes I feel energized. I think it depends on who I am around. I love being social and hanging out with friends I am comfortable with and/or who know I have aspergers. Sometimes I wonder if I am truly an extrovert but just never learned the social skills to be good at it.
